requirements.description: Host-only geometry and model use need neither loader, BPF compiler nor privilege. Features, errors, resource bounds and intended owner traits are public.

Allocate checked `align_up(value_size, 8) × possible_cpu_count` for per-CPU I/O; validate map metadata, key/value ABI and every actual consumer stride before syscall. Parsed/model topology cannot authorize a lengthless kernel copy; use opaque internally acquired live topology and refuse unauthenticated source/change. Capability state, evidence stage, hazard outcome and runtime authority are distinct. Bind cached observations to object/profile/context; no diagnostic receipt can mint authority.

Attachment plans preserve file authority and offset-cookie associations, use at most `2n−1` attempts for nonempty n-site split isolation, and obey caller error policy without retrying terminal denial/resource failures.

Every partial attachment has a terminal disposition: returned active owner, retired, pending or unresolved custody. Retain the original file through native retirement; caller-owned persistent pool permits remain charged for active, uncertain, pending and orphaned effects. Drop is no cleanup proof.

Ring arithmetic is checked, modular wrap is explicit, BUSY is pending, fixed-tail crossing is an error, and bounded drain never grants quiescence. Preserve the backend's documented mmap memory ordering and sole-consumer authority.
Copied staging survives callback-source mutation; a short destination retries the same record once delivered. Preserve separate received/delivered/held/malformed/dropped conservation and error tails.
Writer ownership names program, site, CPU lane, guard and architecture. Different programs on one CPU do not share an unprotected slot. Guard refusal has its own miss channel.

Insertion identity uses one valid ownership marker; zero identity values stay valid. Independent preallocated diagnostic storage survives primary-map full failure; a cap of 255 is a degradation indication, not an exact event count.
Producer task/exec identity distinguishes birth/thread/exec success/failure, session domains and exhaustion; poll/PID/starttime tracking is never upgraded into this protocol.
Adapt an existing BTF parser; preserve bounded wrapper/type/member/prototype queries and base/module type and string domains. Equal names or sizes alone do not establish identity or map type linkage.
Loader adapters stay narrow, independently optional and validated on exact emitted objects. Track upstream patches separately; no source-green/metadata-green result establishes live support.

Each advertised profile ships public developer cases, fixtures, a source-free installed operator path and at least two independent downstream package consumers of its actual APIs. Required old/current/affected kernel cells are selected before availability discovery. Product migrations are deferred.
Wrong map-kind operations refuse before extent arithmetic, allocation or native lookup; configuration failure preserves native state and generation or returns poisoned/unresolved ownership.

Preserve issue provenance, source/toolchain pins, exact effective command/CPU/features, loaded backend identity, output hashes and expected layer-specific outcome. No implicit compiler installation; persistent executor jobs own descendant scope and output-root reservations across timeout.

Profile admission checks decoded final instructions and architecture/endianness/ABI; CPU preset names alone cannot broaden support. Separate ISA, helpers/maps/kfuncs, loader relocation, BTF shape, attach and behavior requirements.

Used-result RMW tests check old returned and new stored values for each width/op, independent arithmetic, unused-result/CAS controls and selected fixed/unfixed compilers. Concurrent-map/ordering claims have separate live schedules.
AtomicLoad compile refusal/ordinary-load/acquire-load distinctions are tested against explicit features. No volatile substitution or classifier that calls compiler failure a verifier rejection.
Final mixed Rust/C outputs retain valid debug metadata/BTF/BTF.ext with meaningful function/map types through every transformation. Exit zero or parser replay is insufficient.

Object graph transformations are restricted, relocation/callback-aware, and fail closed on unsupported shape. Named stack/linkage/padding/prologue rules preserve old and new kernel workarounds with mutation controls.

Load, verifier/JIT acceptance, execution correctness, concurrency, performance and cleanup are separate judgments on exact final object bytes. Freeze oldest/current/affected/backport cells before execution.
Upstream patches/workarounds have individual scope, application hash/preimage, test, upstream status and expiration evidence. Merged source alone never retires a workaround or updates a consumer pin.
Shipped tools and fixtures run from source archives and an installed offline closure, plus downstream actual-library/backend users. No testkit-private resolver copy can certify another candidate.

`scopebase-sdk` composes public components with explicit Cargo features. Rust edition 2021; proposed MSRV 1.88.0, requiring actual qualification. Default host build has no BPF/native/Mojo tool invocation or privilege changes. Independent downstream default and supported feature-union builds prove this. |

Profile declares required capabilities and admitted effects before probing environments. `Unsupported`, `Denied`, `Unknown` and `Incompatible` remain distinct. A successful refusal case never upgrades capability support; imported reports cannot construct runtime authority. |

Resource configuration separates input bytes, retained bytes, visited work, live owners, diagnostics and elapsed wait. Invalid/zero/overflowing limits are refused before effects. Time allowance is an observation deadline, not guaranteed syscall interruption or cleanup. |

App context integrates capture epoch/window metadata and component bindings while leaving application state machines, scopes, privacy and session closure local. A summary carries the actual component's receipt strength; no SDK `close()` or `drain()` may synthesize quiescence. |

Diagnostics are opt-in, bounded, structured and inert by default. No implicit logging or raw captured bytes; byte paths use safe escaping in display. Exceeding diagnostic count/byte allowance produces an explicit truncation count, never silent disappearance or arithmetic wrap. |

The owned-workload file observer is a genuine non-crypto application of the Linux and capture components. It observes held descriptors, independently generated A/B file contents and path replacement; it reports effects, limits, inconclusive states and final owner disposition. It neither scans unrelated processes nor changes credentials, limits, signals or namespaces. |

An owned fixture ledger establishes expectations independently of production reads and capture reducers. Positive A and active negative B both execute. A path-reopen mutant, unknown-as-zero mutant and fabricated complete-session mutant each fail their intended assertion after verified setup. |

The standalone starter builds outside the monorepo against packaged artifacts and invokes the developer conformance API on its own linked production adapter. It includes application-owned host and optional BPF orchestration examples, not copied loader/tracker implementations. |

A selected non-crypto BPF observer recipe uses the existing Aya backend through `scopebase-bpf`; its independent workload, final ELF/BTF inspection, live positive/negative and cleanup gates are required for complete SDK acceptance. Its build/run is opt-in for users and is not a default Rust dependency. Host-only package readiness remains a separate submilestone. |

Two concurrent SDK host contexts have independent epochs, limits, fixture roots, diagnostics and owner outcomes. No hidden global lock, signal handler or resource registry is introduced. Shared backend resources require explicit adapter ownership. |

Packaging includes versioned profile documentation, developer conformance calls and an installed operator route from the delivered artifacts. Offline checks work after staging prerequisites with no donor/monorepo checkout. Exact dependency versions/features and executable/library hashes bind results. |

SDK compatibility, feature additions, MSRV policy, provenance and donor issue/removal records are published with the package. Completion maps every advertised operation to a required case and qualified cell; missing required cells remain incomplete. MG migration readiness is reported separately. |

Author a small versioned neutral corpus independently of production encoders/reducers: framing, integer boundaries, unknown/zero, epoch mismatch, quality dependencies, short output/retry and cleanup outcomes. Rust/C/Mojo clients share expected semantics, not generated observed answers. |

Audit the actually consumed libbpf-mojo source/bundle separately from main/joint candidates and preserve all branch/WIP evidence. Report API, ownership, tracepoint/map/test-run scope, source-only tests and missing emitted/live/installed qualification per operation. No donor edits or implicit upgrades follow. |

Deliver copied-record retry regression additions against the existing libbpf reader: repeated short output, source mutation, EINTR, malformed/discard/pressure, held once and conservation. A direct-pointer or consume-on-short mutant must fail the held-byte assertion. |

Deliver transactional configuration tests against the existing bridge: failed autoload/target update leaves native configuration and generation unchanged; success changes generation once; stale views refuse. Fault setup and independent native observation prove transactionality. |

Deliver map buffer geometry tests using possible CPUs including offline lanes, eight-byte alignment, checked multiplication, exact consumer stride, bloom distinction, alias/short output refusal and untouched error output. Host mocks and actual live map checks remain separately labeled. |

Deliver close/release/loader-lifetime tests: child references keep parent/library alive, `EBUSY` preserves usable owner, delayed cleanup remains unresolved, short retries do not duplicate delivery, and every permitted disposal path retires exactly once. Single-thread scope remains explicit. |

MojoBPF integration consumes standard ELF/BTF through the existing libbpf-mojo/libbpf boundary. Actual object checks cover map BTF, relocations, section/call/helper shape and version/profile binding. Verifier success, live semantics and cleanup are separate required gates for an advertised recipe. |

`scopebase-ffi` exports only the pure capture-validation operation specified below, justified by independently usable C and Mojo validation clients. No BPF loader, syscall wrapper, foreign application reducer or custom ring protocol is added. Rust packages stay usable without FFI. |

The ABI freezes version, widths, enum codes, ownership, alignment, alias rules, buffer retry, error precedence, allocation, threading, fork/exec and panic behavior. Header/Rust/C/Mojo layout tests and negative controls enforce the same contract. |

Sanitizer, fuzz and independent cross-language tests cover unaligned input, malformed/overflowing lengths, integer extremes, bad versions/reserved fields, duplicate/unknown fields, partial output and concurrent disjoint calls. Invalid raw pointers remain caller contract violations, not catchable parse errors. |

Installed C and Mojo clients work offline from staged release artifacts without donor/monorepo source, locate the intended shared library, report ABI/library/build identity and run positive and negative vectors. System ABI/toolchain prerequisites are explicit and qualified. |

Deliver per-file license/provenance, versioned package support/patch register, operation-specific qualification matrix and MG handoff. Source/vector/host/object/live/installed tiers are reported independently; future C/Mojo use is planned work until these gates pass. |
